messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: backward compatibility
parts:
It sounds like RStan 2.8 changed the way things worked
given the rant on the user's list. Now if this is just
an issue of some minor graphics output, I'm less concerned
than if some of the estimation functions changed signatures
in a way that's not backward compatible.

The problem is that users build up workflows based on
an existing API, so when it changes, the rug gets pulled out
from under them.

I very very much want to stick to transparent semantic versioning:

major.minor.patch

New features get a minor++, bug fix releases patch++, and
anything that breaks backward compatiblity, major++.

That is, I don't think we should break backward compatiblity
except for major releases. Is there a way to retrofit things
so that API alls from RStan 2.7 continue to work in 2.8?

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: backward compatibility
parts:
On Monday, September 21, 2015 at 2:45:31 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
It sounds like RStan 2.8 changed the way things worked
given the rant on the user's list.  Now if this is just
an issue of some minor graphics output, I'm less concerned
than if some of the estimation functions changed signatures
in a way that's not backward compatible.

It was the (lack of automatic) layout of traceplots, not even the way the graphics were computed, much less the way the posterior was drawn from. Moreover, I don't think we should really be in the layout business; as long as we can provide an easy way to extract the information from the stanfit object that needs to go into a plot, then users can lay things out however they want (with much more flexibility in ggplot2 than in base graphics).

Ben

:-) We could repeat Andrew's dictum that you not include
things you don't want people to study. And if you really wanted
78 traceplots, I could imagine an 8 x 10 grid that let you see
their general outlines.

I don't usually want to look at more than a handful
of them to see if the chains are correlated and how fast
adaptation is working across parameters.

- Bob
